personal.title: Personal
personal.summary: I want to understand how things work and how they can be improved. For me, that way of thinking began with strategy games.
personal.story: When I played board and card games as a child, I usually wanted to win. First I had to understand the rules, consider my options, decide which goal mattered most and work out which move would make sense in the long run. Eventually, I noticed that I asked the same questions when facing completely different problems. I enjoy recognising the systems underneath, understanding them and finding solutions of my own. That made studying computer science a natural choice.
personal.technicalText: I have not chosen a specialisation yet. So far, I am most interested in systems and optimisation, software development and mathematics. I like software development because it lets me put my own ideas into practice. Mathematics fascinates me because its methods can be applied to so many different problems.
personal.beyondText: I still enjoy board and card games. I designed one card game myself and continue to play it today. It is a personal creative project, not a computer science project.

projects.title: Personal Projects
projects.summary: I also work on my own ideas outside university. Sometimes I want to build an application, and sometimes I want to investigate a mathematical question. I am interested not only in the finished result but also in understanding the problems along the way. Here I share work that I have spent more time on.

app.title: Nutrition Tracking App
app.teaser: I spent about half a year developing an app of my own with Flutter. It can record and analyse different personal metrics. I wanted to design the workflows myself and avoid restricting users to one fixed way of entering data.
app.imageAlt: Illustrative phone placeholder, not a real screenshot of my app
app.detailLead: The app includes a customisable home screen, a calendar, a QR scanner, statistics, and my own system for quick or combined entries, among other features.
detailPoints: I wanted to create an app that could adapt to different habits. There should not be just one fixed way to enter each type of measurement.
I built the app myself with Dart and Flutter, connecting the features step by step. A lot of work went into the different ways of entering data and analysing it afterwards.
I enjoyed thinking through the application as a whole rather than just programming individual features. Every new idea came with decisions and dependencies that I had to consider.

I underestimated how important it is to test complicated screens early. There are still bugs in the current version. The statistics view crashes when opened. If I started again, I would plan systematic testing much earlier.

math.title: Prime Numbers and Mathematical Experiments
math.teaser: For several years, I have investigated mathematical questions in my spare time, especially in number theory. I write programs, test conjectures and develop my own models. They often lead to new questions, even when the original idea does not work.
math.imageAlt: Typographic display of prime numbers as a placeholder for a future visualisation
math.detailLead: I have explored questions relating to Goldbach, Legendre, prime k-tuples and the Riemann hypothesis. These are my own investigations, not proofs of open conjectures.
detailPoints: I am interested in patterns that seem simple at first but are difficult to explain. With prime numbers in particular, I wanted to see what regularities might exist and how possible connections could be tested.

I mainly worked with Python and have more recently tried C++ as well. Alongside calculations, I developed abstract models, including my Fake Prime-Wheel. I examine what is true within that model and do not assume that those properties automatically hold for actual primes.
I most enjoy moving between an idea, a mathematical argument and a program that tests it. Often, the results quickly show which assumption needs more thought.

Not every observation from a model can be transferred to the original problem. Some of my own attempts failed for exactly that reason. They taught me the importance of precise definitions, counterexamples and keeping experiments separate from proofs.
